A refined adult anime face drawn to her own FACE line below — her own eye size and shape, nose, mouth and jaw, not one shared default face; delicately drawn eyelids. Fine subtle linework, smooth skin shading and softly blended gradients. Layered flowing hair with carefully drawn strands and delicate highlights. Highly detailed clothing and accessories with convincing fabric weave, stitching, folds, seams, buckles and material-specific reflections. Combine stylized anime facial features with richly rendered dimensional clothing. Use luminous midtones, restrained highlights on clothing, and a delicate pastel palette. Her skin has a glossy sheen — smooth, bright specular highlights on her shoulders, collarbones, chest, arms and thighs, a polished lustrous finish over her skin tone, never wet or oily. Apply this style only to the person, preserving the separately specified character design, pose and setting.

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her wearing the costume chosen in SCENE — a daring adult costume version of her source creature, as worn to a costume party, convention or photo shoot. In this cut her species shows in the outfit itself: its recognisable colours, shapes and parts. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; the Framing in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

CROP: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame. This crop wins over every other line — pose, outfit, props and activity details apply only to the part that shows, and the outfit reads through its visible neckline, straps, fabric and colour. The lens sets perspective only, never how much of her shows. Do not widen the shot to fit them in. An arm or leg that crosses the edge runs naturally on past it — never cut off, shortened or fading out inside the image.

SCENE (chosen):

Activity: waiting in the queue outside, a short jacket over her shoulders
Outfit: a daring adult costume version of Venomoth itself — pale purple, purple colours; its pale purple moth-like wings, three-point crest, lepidopteran insect, tiny, whitish legs rebuilt as costume pieces (ears or headband, hood, tail, gloves, fabric prints), never painted on her own skin, cut as a high-cut bodysuit with sheer thigh-high tights

Framing: Chest-up framing focused on the face, shoulders and expression with a small amount of setting.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
Expression: raised inner brows, darting or averted eyes, mouth slightly open, faint blush across the cheeks and nose
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more shoulder, neckline and upper-back exposure inside the crop; cover the chest
action_level: balanced — a readable moment of gentle movement, not a ratio of multiple images
separates_preference: prefer separates — prefer separate top and bottom unless outfit is explicitly specified

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely into the costume SCENE describes. From the attached image take only her face and hair — not its armor, garment, jewelry, hair ornaments or background. The costume must read at first glance as that creature's look, rebuilt as a glamorous adult outfit; she is a real woman in a costume — never the creature itself, its face on her face, fur or scales on her skin, a logo or readable text.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same.

ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no creature beside her, no text, no lettering, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions — about 7.5 heads tall, her head in proportion to her shoulders and body. No extra limbs; her worn features are costume, never extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame.

HANDS: natural human hands.

HAND TASK: her hands act naturally for the pose and scene; any idle hand rests in a relaxed, anatomically plausible position. Natural occlusion is allowed; do not force every hand or finger into view.
